brief.headline: Close the ₹16.09 L gap to Mars Plastics pricing and free up ₹10.63 L cash by moving to 30-day terms.

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics on the 30 ml HDPE bottle (₹1.38/NOS) and the 28 mm PP cap (₹0.81/NOS), and bring the 60 ml bottle down to ₹2.20/NOS in line with Cincorp.
priceAsk.basis: We pay ₹1.65/NOS for the 30 ml bottle when Mars sells it at ₹1.38/NOS — a 19.6% gap. The 28 mm cap has an 11.1% gap (₹0.90 vs ₹0.81). The market asking price for a similar 28 mm cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so ₹0.81 is well within market range. Close these gaps and we save ₹16.09 L a year.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days after receipt.

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue or cash position. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend is meaningful but not enormous. With no visibility into their health, the smartest play is to use the price gap and the strength of our alternates — not to squeeze blind. We have five credible second sources ready (Mold-Tek, Hitech, Pearl, Manjushree, Pravesha), plus six maker/recycler leads to qualify, so we're not locked in. Push firmly on price and terms, and make it clear we're actively lining up a backup.

evidence.point: We overpay by ₹16.09 L a year versus the best prices we already pay other suppliers.
The 30 ml HDPE bottle costs us ₹1.65/NOS here, but Mars Plastics supplies it at ₹1.38/NOS — a 19.6% gap costing us ₹11.74 L a year.
The 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.90/NOS from them, ₹0.81/NOS from Mars — an 11.1% gap worth ₹4.23 L a year.
Market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with room to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, so our ₹0.90 is market-fair but Mars's ₹0.81 is achievable.
Cutting payment terms from 45 days to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L cash for us.
We spend ₹1.29 Cr a year with them — enough volume to expect competitive pricing.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, specializes in pharma bottles and caps, revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B (65/100) — a strong second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, and pharma packaging — robust and profitable, direct fit for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed company with broad moulded and blow-moulded packaging capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Premier Plastic's financials aren't public, so we're negotiating blind — watch for any hints of cash strain (late deliveries, quality slips) that would make a hard push risky.
We have no incumbent alternate supplier today for rigid plastic packaging — every name on our list is a lead we still need to qualify and audit before we can credibly threaten to switch.
The top SKU (30 ml bottle) drives ₹11.74 L of the ₹16.09 L gap — if they won't move on that one item, the saving shrinks fast.

Cutting 15 days of payment terms is worth ₹10.63 L to us, but it tightens their cash by the same amount — if they're fragile (we can't tell), pushing too hard on both price and terms at once might backfire.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹16.09 lakh more a year than we pay Mars Plastics and others for the same bottles and caps — let's close that gap and move to 30-day terms so we can keep this partnership competitive.
